introduction: On this Sunday, David has the chance to kill King Saul, who is hunting him, but he spares his life. In the Gospel, Jesus says, Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, be merciful as your Father is merciful. Paul tells us that we will bear the image of the heavenly man. Let us ask for a heart that loves even those who hurt us.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord is merciful and gracious. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may be a sign of the Father's mercy in a world of revenge and division. Let us pray to the Lord.
For nations at war and peoples divided by hatred: that they may find the way of reconciliation. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have hurt us, and those we have hurt: that God may bless them and heal the wounds between us. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who find it hard to forgive: that the grace of God may soften their hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be merciful as our Father is merciful. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Merciful Father, you are kind even to the ungrateful and the wicked. Teach us to love our enemies, to forgive and to give generously, so that we may be your children. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Be merciful
reflection.body:
David is on the run. King Saul, jealous and afraid, is hunting him with three thousand men. One night David and his companion Abishai creep into Saul's camp and find him asleep, his spear stuck in the ground beside his head. Abishai sees the perfect opportunity: "God has delivered up your enemy into your hand today." But David refuses: "Don't destroy him, for who can stretch out his hand against the LORD's anointed, and be guiltless?" He takes the spear and the water jar and leaves. He will not take revenge.

In the Gospel, Jesus asks something even harder. "But I tell you who hear: love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, and pray for those who mistreat you." He gives a simple rule: "As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them." And he shows why ordinary kindness is not enough: "If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them."

The reason is God himself: "he is kind toward the unthankful and evil." So Jesus says, "Therefore be merciful, even as your Father is also merciful." We are called to love like God loves. And there is a promise: "Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over."

This is not natural to us. We cannot do it by willpower alone. Paul tells us that as we have borne the image of Adam, "let's also bear the image of the heavenly." Christ's grace makes possible what seems impossible.

This week, think of one person who has hurt you. Pray for them by name each day. And if you can, do one good thing for them, or at least refuse to speak badly of them. That is how the love of enemies begins.
